- For a single API call that submits 1 document with 20 candidate labels, how many "units" would we be billed for?
- If we batch 50 documents in one request (each with variable candidate counts), how is that billed? Is there a per-request minimum?
- Example invoice line items: can you share a dummy invoice showing line-level descriptions (e.g., classifier scoring, context tokens, model surcharge, discount line)?
- Any guidance on discounts at 10M, 50M, 200M scored items per month?

Mike —

Thanks for the clear asks and the sample payload. Short answers up front, then I pulled in Aditya and Marcus to confirm rates/discounts and to draft a one-page sample invoice.

- Unit counting: each candidate scored is counted as one scoring-unit. So 1 document with 20 candidates = 20 scoring-units.
- Batching: total scoring-units = sum of all candidate counts in the batch. No per-request minimum. We meter at the scoring-unit level after request is processed.
- Tokens/context: any tokenized context used to evaluate a candidate (prompt/context tokens) are billed separately under "context tokens" at our standard token rates and are measured per-request.
- Example invoice & discounts: Aditya — can you confirm the baseline list pricing and typical tiered discounts for the volumes Mike listed? Marcus — can you attach a one-page sample invoice we can send to procurement?

I'll follow up with the PDF and a short explanatory blurb for procurement.

Best,
Sofia

Folks — a couple clarifications to include in the procurement note: 

1) Baseline list price (hosted API, classifier/rerank scoring): 
   - $0.35 per 1,000 scoring-units (scoring-unit = 1 candidate scored) for Standard models
   - $0.90 per 1,000 scoring-units for Large/High-accuracy models (calls that choose a model with explicit surcharge)

2) Token billing: context tokens billed separately at $0.002 per 1,000 tokens (this is illustrative; show as separate line).

3) Batch behavior: if you send 50 documents with average 12 candidates each, total units = 600. The request is atomically metered after processing — no additional per-request fee.

4) Discounts: tiered off monthly scored-units (applied to scoring-units line only):
   - 10M+ units/month: 10% off list
   - 50M+ units/month: 18% off list
   - 200M+ units/month: custom enterprise pricing (we typically move to a committed capacity/Reserved plan with guaranteed throughput and a flat per-month fee)

5) Invoice sample: include line items and a discount line. We can show a punchy example: 
   - Classifier scoring (Standard model): 600,000 units @ $0.35 / 1,000 = $210.00
   - Context tokens: 3,000,000 tokens @ $0.002 / 1,000 = $6.00
   - Model surcharge (Large model usage): $45.00
   - Subtotal: $261.00
   - Volume discount (10%): -$26.10
   - Tax: $0.00 (example)
   - Total due: $234.90

Marcus — please craft the one-pager and include the CSV sample mapping to units for transparency.

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Clarify scoring unit metering and sample invoice for classifier endpoint

Mike — quick answers: 

- Streaming / persistent connections: billing is still based on scoring-units processed. Keeping an open socket has no metering delta; we only invoice for scoring activity (per candidate scored) and any token usage.
- Committed usage: at 50M+ we typically propose a Reserved capacity contract — commercial teams move to a flat monthly commitment that buys an effective per-unit rate (e.g., equivalent to ~25-30% off list depending on commitment length). Reserved comes with throughput SLOs (e.g., sustained X RPS, burst to Y RPS) and an SLA. Exact numbers are negotiated per account and included in the contract.

Happy to set a 30-min call to go over Reserved capacity options if procurement prefers.

-Aditya
